task: Pick up the box in the other room, but do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) hard is exactly the command 'Pick up the box in the other room'. Precedence(door_open, key_lost) hard captures 'do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once': the ban on key_lost (a drop of the key while the door is still closed, per its definition) holds until the first door_open and lifts after it, which is the 'until' reading; key_lost's own definition already encodes the 'while the door is closed' condition. Both clauses are hard as worded ('do not' is categorical, no preference cue), all identifiers are declared, and no clause is redundant or added — the machine's final state u1 is reached only via target_picked_up and rejecting state u2 fires on key_lost before door_open, matching the clauses.
